feature: Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app
audit_feature: Auditor desktop workbench
codex_behavior: The desktop experience brings projects, chats, agent activity, files, execution tools, review, configuration and execution-location choices into one workspace. Available features differ by operating system, account and client release.
trigger: The auditor opens a workspace or starts a task.
audit_action: Coordinate audit work through conversation while keeping source material, workpapers, calculations and agent progress inspectable beside it.
outputs: Links to existing files and tools
auditor_control: Choose the task and execution location, inspect changes, steer work, and open the same saved artifacts in external editors.
example: Ask for a loan-interest reconciliation, inspect its workbook beside the chat, then continue reviewing that workbook in Excel.
adaptation_boundary: Retain the working experience while replacing developer emphasis with audit materials. Embedded editing depth and platform parity require validation; a desktop workspace alone does not establish formal audit records.

subfeatures.audit: Conversation beside evidence and workpapers
Visible analysis jobs and inspectable execution
Review changed audit work and its supporting calculations
Configure the same assistance mechanisms around audit work

audit_enhancements.change: Show workbook ranges, document passages and evidence references beside the conversation.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors review work in units that differ from code lines.

audit_enhancements.change: Provide an explicit open-in-existing-tool path for supported artifacts.
audit_enhancements.why: Review must continue in established applications without replacing the underlying work files.

audit_feature: Audit workspaces and focused work conversations
codex_behavior: Projects group files, instructions and chats; local projects can attach folders. Each chat retains its own transcript. Navigation supports search, renaming, pinning and archival. CLI and IDE project context follow their directory or workspace.
trigger: Start a new assignment, standalone investigation or conversation within an existing workspace.
audit_action: Group related audit work and start separate conversations for distinct outcomes, with explicit access to the relevant files and guidance.
auditor_control: Select attached folders, rename or pin recurring work, and archive or restore completed conversations.
example: Keep rate-change testing, borrower communications review and report drafting in separate chats under the same assignment.
adaptation_boundary: A workspace can support ad hoc work or a formal engagement. Folder organisation and pinning do not themselves grant access or enforce confidentiality; primary-folder instruction discovery needs explicit treatment.

subfeatures.audit: Standalone audit question without creating an engagement
Separate workstreams sharing selected materials
Related evidence and working-file locations with explicit guidance scope

subfeatures.codex: Search, pin, rename, archive and restore
subfeatures.audit: Find and organise current and completed audit conversations

audit_enhancements.change: Use assignment, client and reporting-period labels while retaining standalone tasks.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors must distinguish related work without forcing every request into an engagement.

audit_enhancements.change: Show which instructions and folders belong to the current task.
audit_enhancements.why: Similar files from different periods or clients can otherwise be mistaken for the applicable material.

audit_feature: Auditor command-line and batch work client
codex_behavior: The CLI supports interactive investigation, planning, file edits, tool execution and review within a directory. Non-interactive codex exec can run scripted tasks and emit structured events for other processes to consume.
trigger: An auditor or analyst starts an interactive command, or an authorised job invokes a saved task.
audit_action: Offer the same audit assistance through a terminal for technical auditors, data analysts and repeatable batch jobs.
auditor_control: Set working directory, execution scope and requested output; interrupt interactive work or review batch results before relying on them.
example: An IT auditor runs a saved access-review procedure against an approved directory export and receives an exceptions file.
adaptation_boundary: Keep the CLI as a legitimate surface rather than forcing all auditors into it. Installed analysis tools, input formats and event consumers determine what an individual job can do.

subfeatures.audit: Interactive investigation of an audit folder
Reusable headless audit jobs
Machine-readable job progress and results
Continue eligible work through another execution surface

audit_enhancements.change: Accept named audit procedures and structured procedure parameters through the command surface.
audit_enhancements.why: Repeated analyses need explicit period, population and criteria inputs rather than only a freeform prompt.

audit_feature: Audit task command and session controls
codex_behavior: CLI and slash commands manage sessions, plans, goals, models, permissions, tools and review. Commands also expose context compaction, configuration, keymaps and reconnect controls. Maturity varies: some cloud and remote-control commands remain experimental.
trigger: The auditor invokes a task control through a command, shortcut or equivalent interface action.
audit_action: Expose the same task-management operations using audit-friendly labels while preserving access for power users.
auditor_control: Explicitly choose operations that change execution, permissions, context or task direction.
example: Pause analysis, inspect its status, revise the plan, change the model effort, then resume the same investigation.
adaptation_boundary: Command names are not audit controls by themselves. Preserve actual semantics and maturity labels; do not imply experimental remote or cloud commands are universally available.

subfeatures.audit: Manage investigation sessions and alternate approaches
Control a work approach, objective and review pass
Control effort and inspect available working context
Adjust permitted analysis actions within policy

subfeatures.codex: Agents, subagents, apps, plugins and hooks
subfeatures.audit: Manage assistance and extension mechanisms
Select identity and working scope
Personalise controls without changing audit methods
Recover or move supported sessions

audit_enhancements.change: Expose audit-friendly labels and descriptions for task controls while retaining power-user commands.
audit_enhancements.why: Users should understand execution, review and context operations without knowing developer terminology.

audit_feature: Audit agent and workstream command center
codex_behavior: The command center lists chats and their status on a shared local or remote server and lets a user switch into them. It is a coordination surface separate from spawning delegated subagents.
trigger: The auditor opens the task command center to inspect ongoing work.
audit_action: Provide one place to see active audit investigations, identify work awaiting input, and enter the relevant conversation.
auditor_control: Choose which investigation to enter and respond to its questions; visibility remains bounded by accessible work.
example: Move between a loan recalculation, an access review and report preparation without losing each conversation's context.
adaptation_boundary: Preserve the distinction between finding a running task and directing a delegated agent. A shared server list does not by itself provide organisation-wide audit portfolio management or new access rights.

subfeatures.audit: Accessible audit workstreams by execution server
Identify work running, finished or requiring attention
Resume the chosen investigation in context

audit_enhancements.change: Display assignment and tested period beside each workstream's status.
audit_enhancements.why: Auditors need to distinguish similarly named investigations across clients and periods.

audit_feature: Assistance inside an auditor's working application
codex_behavior: The IDE extension provides Codex conversation and tools within supported code editors, using the open workspace and selected context. Its integration, orchestration and review features differ from desktop and CLI clients.
trigger: The auditor opens an available extension in a supported working tool and asks about selected material.
audit_action: Bring conversation and contextual assistance beside the work already open in an auditor's application, using supported integration mechanisms.
auditor_control: Select the material and requested action, inspect proposed changes, and choose whether to apply them.
example: Select an exceptions table in a supported Excel extension and ask the agent to explain differences or prepare follow-up questions.
adaptation_boundary: This directly mirrors the IDE-extension experience. It is additional to shared-file assistance; basic use of saved Office files does not depend on building an add-in. Live selection and unsaved state require explicit host support.

subfeatures.audit: Conversation beside current audit work
Current artifact context under host permissions
Ask about a selected range, paragraph or slide
Inspect and accept supported changes without leaving the working tool

audit_enhancements.change: Map host selection to stable range, paragraph or slide references where the host supports them.
audit_enhancements.why: Contextual assistance must identify the precise material being discussed.

audit_enhancements.change: Expose whether context is saved file state or live application state.
audit_enhancements.why: The agent and auditor must not unknowingly work from different versions.

audit_feature: Remote audit execution workspace
codex_behavior: Cloud tasks run in prepared remote workspaces with selected repositories, dependencies and tools. Work can continue while the local computer sleeps, and users can inspect results and follow up on the task.
trigger: The auditor starts or delegates an eligible task to a prepared cloud environment.
audit_action: Execute an audit analysis or document task remotely and return its artifacts and task history for review.
outputs: Proposed changes or a review package
auditor_control: Select what is provided to the remote task, follow progress, stop work and review its returned outputs.
example: Run an overnight reconciliation on an approved extract and review the exceptions the following morning.
adaptation_boundary: A cloud task cannot assume access to the auditor's local Excel session, local-only folders, VPN or browser sign-in. Residency, tools and permissions depend on the selected execution route.

subfeatures.audit: Reusable audit execution environment
Scoped materials for a remote analysis
Long remote analyses independent of the workstation
Review findings and request further testing in context

audit_enhancements.change: Make the supplied dataset version and procedure version visible in remote results.
audit_enhancements.why: The reviewer must know what an unattended analysis actually examined.

audit_feature: Remote steering and review of audit work
codex_behavior: Supported mobile and remote clients can start, steer, approve and review tasks running on a connected host or in Cloud. Execution retains the chosen host's files, tools and permissions; the mobile device is a control surface.
trigger: The auditor connects from a supported remote device to accessible work.
inputs: Connected execution host or cloud task
audit_action: Let the auditor monitor and steer an investigation away from the workstation while preserving its execution context.
outputs: Continued work on the execution host
auditor_control: Choose the host and task, inspect what an approval authorises, and interrupt or revise the work.
example: During a site visit, check an ongoing reconciliation and tell the agent to investigate one flagged branch further.
adaptation_boundary: Phone access does not move all data or execution onto the phone. Mobile remote workflows and the experimental CLI remote-control command have different maturity and platform conditions.

subfeatures.audit: Direct audit work from another device
Respond to scoped requests and inspect findings
Retain the authorised data and tool environment
Move an eligible investigation with explicit context transfer

audit_enhancements.change: Present concise findings with accessible supporting evidence on the remote review surface.
audit_enhancements.why: An auditor away from the desk needs enough context to steer responsibly.

audit_feature: Physical controls for audit task navigation
codex_behavior: Codex Micro is a limited-run input device whose keys and other controls can reflect chat status and invoke desktop actions, skills, voice and navigation. Availability depends on hardware, companion software and operating-system permissions.
trigger: The auditor presses or turns an assigned physical control.
audit_action: Offer optional physical shortcuts to switch investigations, dictate instructions, invoke a procedure or inspect a task needing attention.
auditor_control: Choose bindings and keep the meaning of consequential commands visible before using them.
example: Bind keys to three active assignments and use a voice control to add an observation during a walkthrough.
adaptation_boundary: This is retained in the feature mirror as an optional peripheral. It does not require designing new hardware, and a physical approval key cannot establish professional sign-off semantics by itself.

subfeatures.audit: Physical indicators for active audit tasks
Shortcuts to configured procedures and work controls
Navigate work and dictate observations

audit_enhancements.change: Name bindings with the audit task and action they invoke.
audit_enhancements.why: A shortcut must remain understandable when several assignments are active.

audit_feature: Choice of working location and isolated analysis copies
codex_behavior: A task can run in its local project directory, an isolated Git worktree, or a remote workspace created from a published environment. Supported handoff changes where work runs and which working files it uses.
trigger: The auditor starts a task or moves eligible work to another environment.
audit_action: Offer direct work on current artifacts, an isolated working copy for parallel investigation, or prepared remote execution.
outputs: Task context tied to its environment
auditor_control: Select the environment, understand its data access, and reconcile results before replacing shared working files.
example: Compare two sampling approaches in isolated work areas while retaining the original population extract.
adaptation_boundary: Git worktrees remain usable for suitable versioned material. Applying isolation to complex Office files requires checking copy/version/merge behavior; neither a worktree nor a working copy is an independent confidentiality boundary.

subfeatures.audit: Work on authorised current files
Isolate competing edits or investigation variants
Run with explicitly supplied remote materials
Move eligible work while making context and file changes explicit

audit_enhancements.change: Support isolated copies or versions of supported audit artifacts with explicit reconciliation of changes.
audit_enhancements.why: Office files cannot be assumed to merge like source-code text.

audit_feature: Audit agent execution loop
codex_behavior: The harness maintains turn state, requests model responses, routes tool calls, applies relevant permissions, streams activity and persists supported task history. The model proposes work while tools perform permitted operations.
trigger: An auditor submits a task or a configured task receives an authorised continuation.
audit_action: Use the same iterative loop to inspect evidence, calculate or transform data, inspect results, revise work and explain the outcome.
auditor_control: Steer the objective, set accessible resources, respond to approvals and stop work.
example: Investigate a reconciliation difference by reading extracts, running a calculation, inspecting unmatched items and drafting an explanation.
adaptation_boundary: The audit mirror changes tools, context and procedures while preserving the execution loop. The public harness is separate from model services, hosted integrations and the complete desktop interface.

evidence.label: Open agent harness and client boundary

subfeatures.audit: Reason over evidence and execute authorised analyses
Investigate further based on actual results
Keep actions within the task's authority
Make work inspectable and continuable

audit_enhancements.change: Supply audit procedures, artifact-aware tools and evidence context to the retained execution loop.
audit_enhancements.why: The loop is general-purpose; the relevant criteria and work objects make its assistance useful to auditors.

audit_feature: Concurrent retrieval of independent audit context
codex_behavior: Documented CLI changes allow independent read-only lookups, including skill, memory and conversation-history reads, to run concurrently. This is a retrieval optimisation, separate from delegated subagents and concurrent writes.
trigger: A task needs several independent pieces of context.
audit_action: Retrieve eligible independent guidance and task history concurrently, then combine the returned context for the main investigation.
auditor_control: Choose accessible sources and inspect material used; source permissions remain unchanged by concurrent retrieval.
example: Load the configured reconciliation procedure and the current task's earlier decisions at the same time.
adaptation_boundary: Preserve the narrow documented scope. Do not infer safe simultaneous workbook changes, unrestricted parallel connector requests, or a guarantee that every tool read can execute concurrently.

subfeatures.audit: Retrieve relevant procedures without serial delay
Load eligible prior context alongside instructions
Main investigator reconciles the returned context

audit_enhancements.change: Retain source and assignment scope on retrieved guidance and history.
audit_enhancements.why: Concurrent retrieval must not blend another client's facts or a superseded method into the task.

audit_feature: Persistent audit investigations and work turns
codex_behavior: Threads can be started, read, resumed, forked, listed, archived or deleted through supported interfaces. Turns accept input, stream execution and reach completed, failed or interrupted states while retaining their thread context.
trigger: Start a new investigation or send another instruction to existing work.
audit_action: Maintain a continuing audit conversation across questions, analysis runs, corrections and review responses.
auditor_control: Resume an investigation, fork a different approach, interrupt a turn and manage chat visibility under applicable policy.
example: Resume an inventory investigation when missing count sheets arrive, retaining earlier questions and results.
adaptation_boundary: A chat's current files may have changed since its earlier turn. Transcript persistence, archiving and deletion are distinct from approved workpaper retention or immutable audit records.

subfeatures.audit: Maintain and revisit investigations
Explore another approach while preserving prior conversation
Manage chat lifecycle subject to record policy
Distinguish task outcomes and unfinished analysis

audit_enhancements.change: Associate relied-on outputs with the input versions used in their turn.
audit_enhancements.why: Resuming a conversation against changed evidence should not silently reuse an old conclusion.

audit_feature: Visible and steerable audit execution
codex_behavior: Clients stream messages, tool activity, command output, edits and approval requests. Supported surfaces let users answer questions, send follow-ups, steer or queue instructions, and interrupt the current turn.
trigger: An analysis is running and the auditor observes progress or supplies new direction.
audit_action: Keep analysis visible and let the auditor correct scope, explain context or stop an unsuitable line of work as it develops.
auditor_control: Inspect actual tool results, respond to the agent, and stop the task without assuming already completed actions are undone.
example: During procurement analysis, clarify which cancelled orders belong outside the population and ask the agent to revise the calculation.
adaptation_boundary: Progress narration does not prove an action succeeded. Interruption and queued steering must preserve partial results and make unfinished work clear; behavior depends on the execution path.

subfeatures.audit: Inspect ongoing analysis and artifact changes
Supply missing context or scoped authorisation
Refine the investigation during work
Stop further work and inspect partial outputs

audit_enhancements.change: Explain changed testing scope and identify results affected by a steering correction.
audit_enhancements.why: A revised criterion may invalidate earlier calculations even though the conversation continues.

audit_feature: Reviewable audit task planning
codex_behavior: Supported clients can produce a plan and clarifying questions before making changes, expose a task checklist, and let the user refine the proposed approach. The plan is working guidance generated within the task.
trigger: The auditor asks for an approach before analysis or artifact changes begin.
audit_action: Draft the sequence of work, identify missing evidence and propose checks that the auditor can revise before execution.
auditor_control: Modify scope, methods and stopping conditions, then explicitly move from planning to execution where required.
example: Plan an external-audit account analysis, identifying the assertions, supplied criteria, relevant records, procedure and expected supporting work.
adaptation_boundary: This mirrors planning assistance. A model-generated checklist is not automatically an authorised engagement work program; professional approval requirements come from the applicable practice and record workflow.

subfeatures.audit: Agree the analysis approach before changing work
Resolve scope and missing evidence
Track the proposed testing steps

audit_enhancements.change: Express plans using objective, population, procedure, criteria, expected output and outstanding evidence.
audit_enhancements.why: These elements let an auditor evaluate whether a proposed analysis addresses the question.

audit_feature: Persistent objectives for sustained audit work
codex_behavior: Goals retain an objective, completion criteria and steering context while work continues across turns. Supported controls inspect, edit, pause, resume or clear the goal. Goal state is separate from general memory and reusable instructions.
trigger: The auditor sets a sustained objective with explicit completion conditions.
audit_action: Continue a bounded investigation through repeated analyses until its completion conditions are met, it needs input, or the auditor stops it.
auditor_control: Inspect and revise the objective, pause or resume it, and decide when the evidence supports ending the task.
example: Reconcile the approved inventory extract to its control total and explain material unmatched items within an agreed time or cost allowance.
adaptation_boundary: A persistent goal is not a schedule or an event subscription. Completing a task objective does not itself approve an audit conclusion or authorise scope expansion.

subfeatures.audit: Bounded investigation outcome
Continue eligible work across task turns
Retain control of sustained audit work

audit_enhancements.change: State completion conditions in terms of reconciled populations, explained exceptions or reviewed outputs.
audit_enhancements.why: A finished command or generated report is not necessarily the requested audit outcome.

audit_feature: Concurrent audit work in the background
codex_behavior: Supported clients keep long commands, tasks and delegated work running while users attend to other work. Status views expose active or completed tasks and work needing attention, subject to host and client behavior.
trigger: An auditor starts a longer job or multiple independent workstreams.
audit_action: Run eligible independent audit tasks concurrently and surface their results or requests for input without blocking unrelated work.
auditor_control: Inspect and stop each task, prioritise attention, and review results before relying on them.
example: Run duplicate-payment analysis while separately drafting walkthrough questions from a process narrative.
adaptation_boundary: Background execution depends on host availability and the tools used. Two jobs editing the same workbook need coordination; GUI automation may occupy the foreground rather than allowing simultaneous human use.

subfeatures.audit: Allow large analyses to finish while other work continues
Separate audit procedures running in parallel
Surface results, failures and required input by workstream

audit_enhancements.change: Identify shared-file conflicts and separate analysis output destinations before concurrent edits.
audit_enhancements.why: Parallel audit tasks may otherwise overwrite the same working file.

audit_feature: Understanding an existing audit work folder
codex_behavior: Codex reads and searches relevant workspace files, follows applicable repository instructions and uses attached or path-selected context to explain unfamiliar material. Actual read access depends on the execution environment and permission boundary.
trigger: The auditor asks a question about an existing collection of work or supplies specific files.
inputs: Authorised source documents and data files
audit_action: Find relevant material, explain how files relate, identify procedures and prior work, and ground the task in the existing audit context.
auditor_control: Select sources and scope, inspect cited material, and correct the agent's interpretation.
example: Explain a supplier-onboarding process using its policy, workflow narrative, configuration export and prior workpapers.
adaptation_boundary: File discovery does not prove population completeness or document authenticity. Complex formats require appropriate readers, and saved-file access does not imply visibility into unsaved application state.

subfeatures.audit: Locate and read relevant evidence and workpapers
Apply assignment and method instructions
Explain unfamiliar processes, calculations or data structures
Direct the agent to specific supporting material

audit_enhancements.change: Read supported audit formats and retain references to the relevant sheet, range, page or passage.
audit_enhancements.why: Source-backed explanations require more precise references than a filename alone.

audit_enhancements.change: Report inaccessible or unreadable material separately from searched material.
audit_enhancements.why: An auditor must understand the actual scope of the investigation.

audit_feature: Executable audit analysis and utility work
codex_behavior: Codex can run available commands, scripts and project tools, inspect their output and use results in later reasoning. Execution and file changes remain subject to the relevant environment, sandbox and approval policy.
trigger: An audit task needs calculation, transformation, validation or a supported external utility.
audit_action: Write or use executable analyses to reconcile data, recalculate values, test conditions and produce reviewable results.
auditor_control: Inspect methods and inputs, choose permitted execution, and verify results against known checks or control totals.
example: Recalculate expected payroll amounts from approved inputs and supplied rules, then compare them with the payment extract.
adaptation_boundary: The code engine is general-purpose; audit formulas and rules must come from the task's actual criteria. A successful script exit does not establish correct inputs, methodology or conclusions.

subfeatures.audit: Perform reproducible audit calculations
Use approved data, document and system utilities
Verify analysis and diagnose failed procedures
Refine the test without hiding earlier assumptions

audit_enhancements.change: Retain procedure code, input identifiers, parameters and reconciliation checks with results.
audit_enhancements.why: Another auditor needs to inspect and reperform the calculation.

audit_feature: Programmatic composition of audit tools
codex_behavior: Where enabled, Code Mode lets model-authored JavaScript compose tool calls through an execution host. The public configuration labels the feature under development and off by default, with controls over exposed tool namespaces.
trigger: An enabled task needs to combine several permitted tool operations in a programmatic step.
inputs: Tool definitions exposed to the cell
audit_action: Compose permitted retrieval and analysis operations, transform their results and return the relevant material to the conversation.
auditor_control: Keep effective tool permissions visible, inspect results, and interrupt work through supported controls.
example: Retrieve independent approved extracts, align their identifiers and pass only the exceptions into the next analysis step.
adaptation_boundary: Keep its experimental maturity explicit in the mirror. Programmatic composition does not enlarge tool authority or guarantee cancellation of every nested operation; interruption behavior needs verification on the chosen host.

subfeatures.audit: Compose a bounded audit-tool procedure
Pass authorised results between tools
Restrict which audit tools may be composed
Stop supported execution while reporting partial work

audit_enhancements.change: Preserve provenance through intermediate transformations and composed tool calls.
audit_enhancements.why: A compact programmatic result must remain traceable to the evidence and procedure that produced it.

audit_feature: Create and revise the auditor's actual work files
codex_behavior: Codex creates and changes workspace files and supports inspection of changes through relevant clients. Desktop file surfaces can preview supported outputs; Git-specific actions and terminal review differ from artifact-focused editing experiences.
trigger: The auditor requests a new deliverable or a revision to existing work.
inputs: Existing saved files or output requirements
audit_action: Create or revise supported workbooks, documents, presentations, scripts and other files while retaining their use in existing applications.
auditor_control: Review changes in the workbench or another editor, accept or revise them, and continue assistance after saving external edits.
example: Update a reconciliation workbook and its report narrative, then let the auditor refine both in Excel and Word.
adaptation_boundary: Baseline shared-file work requires no API to the editor. Semantic comparisons, formula preservation, macros, comments and concurrent edits require format-specific verification; Git text diffs do not establish Office-file merge safety.

subfeatures.audit: Generate workpapers, analyses and reports
Revise the auditor's current working artifacts
Review and control changes with format-appropriate support
Keep Excel, Word and PowerPoint in the working flow

audit_enhancements.change: Use format-aware comparisons for supported workbooks, documents and presentations.
audit_enhancements.why: A reviewer needs to see meaningful changes such as formulas, values and narrative revisions.

audit_enhancements.change: Detect external saved edits before applying another change.
audit_enhancements.why: The auditor and agent share artifacts and may modify them through different tools.

audit_feature: Visual material as audit task context
codex_behavior: Supported clients accept image inputs such as screenshots and diagrams. Attachment handling and supported formats vary by client, host and version, including differences in remote and mobile flows.
trigger: The auditor supplies a screenshot, diagram or other supported image.
audit_action: Interpret visible material, relate it to the task and identify what further evidence is needed to test the relevant assertion.
auditor_control: Confirm the image's source and context, inspect the interpretation and supply clearer or authoritative material where needed.
example: Provide a screenshot of an access-administration screen and ask which visible entitlements differ from the supplied approved-role matrix.
adaptation_boundary: A screenshot may omit fields, history or population scope. Visual interpretation does not establish authenticity, completeness or that the visible configuration was active at the relevant time.

subfeatures.audit: Inspect captured application context
Understand a supplied process or system diagram
Provide visual context through supported local or remote surfaces

audit_enhancements.change: Keep image provenance, capture context and interpretation uncertainty beside the analysis.
audit_enhancements.why: Visible content alone does not establish the relevant period or completeness of evidence.

audit_feature: Create explanatory audit visuals
codex_behavior: Supported Codex surfaces can generate or edit images using available image tooling, including a reusable skill. Generated visual files can accompany other work; availability and usage conditions depend on the client and workspace.
trigger: The auditor requests an illustration or a revision to an explanatory visual.
inputs: Source diagram or image where applicable
audit_action: Produce visuals for explanations, presentations and training, keeping them distinct from captured source evidence.
auditor_control: Check wording and depicted relationships, request revisions and decide where the visual will be used.
example: Create a clearly labelled illustration explaining role separation in a procurement process for an advisory presentation.
adaptation_boundary: Retain image generation as a general capability without treating a generated illustration as proof of how a process operates. Exact data charts and validated process models need appropriate source-backed methods.

subfeatures.audit: Create an explanatory audit illustration
Revise an authorised presentation visual
Reuse visual production instructions for audit deliverables

audit_enhancements.change: Label explanatory generated visuals distinctly from captured source material.
audit_enhancements.why: Illustrations used in reports must not be mistaken for observed evidence.

audit_feature: Suggested continuations while writing audit instructions
codex_behavior: Eligible desktop users can receive a suggested continuation while drafting a prompt. Accepting it places text in the composer rather than sending it. The documented beta has account, plan, age and region conditions.
trigger: The auditor types an instruction in an enabled composer.
audit_action: Suggest a continuation that helps the auditor articulate a task, while leaving the complete instruction editable before submission.
auditor_control: Ignore or accept the suggestion, edit it and explicitly send the instruction.
example: While writing a reconciliation request, accept a suggestion to include the relevant reporting period, then correct the date before sending.
adaptation_boundary: A suggested prompt is neither a discovered fact nor permission to execute. Preserve the distinction between accepting draft text and submitting a task; the reference feature remains eligibility-limited beta.

subfeatures.audit: Help formulate an audit request
Retain editable user control before submission
Expose availability rather than assuming universal support

audit_enhancements.change: Keep suggested audit wording editable and distinguish it from submitted instructions.
audit_enhancements.why: Convenient drafting must not silently introduce a criterion or authorisation.

feature: Web search, built-in browser, browser extension, and Computer Use
audit_feature: Research and interact with relevant audit sources and applications
codex_behavior: Codex distinguishes web search, a separate-profile built-in browser, approved extension access to existing browser context, and permitted desktop GUI control. These routes have different session and permission boundaries; Windows GUI control uses the foreground.
trigger: An audit task requires current public information, a web workflow or authorised application interaction.
audit_action: Research criteria, inspect relevant interfaces or carry out scoped application steps through the appropriate available route.
auditor_control: Choose the target and action scope, approve access where needed, inspect consequences and stop the operation.
example: Inspect an authorised vendor-onboarding workflow in a test environment and compare visible approval steps with its documented procedure.
adaptation_boundary: Browser state, GUI state and shell networking are distinct. Treat source content as untrusted; confirm consequential actions and recorded results. Windows foreground use and macOS locked-use conditions are not interchangeable.

subfeatures.audit: Find relevant current criteria and public sources
Inspect public pages and local audit tools
Work with permitted existing tabs and authenticated sources
Observe or operate supported applications when needed
Keep research access separate from authority to change business state

audit_enhancements.change: Capture the source location, observation time and permitted action scope for a workflow observation.
audit_enhancements.why: Reviewers need to know where an observation came from and whether business state was changed.

feature: Browser annotations and site integration API
audit_feature: Point at a specific source passage or application object
codex_behavior: Users can select page content, annotate it and send it with available context to Codex. A site integration API can customise selectable targets and metadata. This is separate from general browser actions and WebMCP tools.
trigger: The auditor selects content in a supported browser surface and adds an instruction.
audit_action: Anchor an audit question or revision request to the material the auditor is viewing, rather than requiring a separate description of its location.
outputs: Follow-up analysis tied to the selected material
auditor_control: Choose the selection, inspect supplied context and state the requested action.
example: Select a clause in an online incident-management procedure and ask how it relates to the proposed walkthrough.
adaptation_boundary: Selection metadata is context, not automatic evidence capture or source authenticity. Website-defined metadata must remain distinguishable from the auditor's instructions; browser annotation does not imply connector write access.

subfeatures.audit: Ask about a particular passage or displayed object
Let supported audit pages identify meaningful selectable records
Provide relevant source context while showing what is supplied

audit_enhancements.change: Carry useful audit references such as policy section or record identifier with selected content when available.
audit_enhancements.why: A later reviewer needs to locate the material behind the question.
